definition: The state agency, within the Department of Business and Industry, that licenses real estate professionals, investigates complaints, and administers Nevada real estate law.
A board appointed by the Governor that adopts regulations, hears disciplinary cases, and sets policy for real estate licensing in Nevada.
The head of the Real Estate Division, who runs day-to-day licensing, investigations and enforcement.
Nevada's real estate license law (Nevada Revised Statutes chapter 645) and the regulations adopted under it (Nevada Administrative Code chapter 645).
A hearing before the Real Estate Commission on a complaint against a licensee, after which the Commission may dismiss or impose discipline.
A money penalty the Commission may impose for violations: up to $10,000 per violation.
A licensee's request that a district court review a final disciplinary decision of the Commission.

term: Real Estate Education, Research and Recovery Fund
definition: A state fund that pays people who won a court judgment against a Nevada licensee for fraud, misrepresentation or deceit in a real estate transaction, up to set limits. It also supports education and research.
For compensation, selling, buying, listing, exchanging, leasing, negotiating, or offering to do so, for someone else. It requires a Nevada real estate license.
Performing licensed real estate acts for others without a license. It's illegal, and the person can't sue to collect a commission.
A Nevada license to perform real estate activities only while associated with and supervised by a licensed broker.
A person who qualifies for a broker license but works under another broker's supervision.
A license that allows a person to operate a real estate brokerage and supervise licensees.
A permit, added to a Nevada real estate license, required to engage in property management.
A permit, added to a Nevada real estate license, required to act as a business broker.
Education from an NRED-approved school required before taking the salesperson exam.
A license status in which the licensee may not perform real estate activities, such as when not associated with a broker.
Education required to renew a Nevada license, including required topics. Most sources cite 36 hours per two-year renewal after the first renewal.
A course new Nevada salespersons must complete during their first year of licensure.
The broker responsible for supervising the licensees associated with the brokerage.
The formal relationship, filed with the Division, that lets a salesperson or broker-salesperson work under a broker.
A broker's separate account for money held for others, kept and recorded as NRS 645.310 and the regulations require.
The Division's authority to inspect and audit a broker's trust records.
The name under which the brokerage is licensed with the Division. Nevada advertising must show it.
Acts listed in Nevada law, such as misrepresentation, commingling, or paying unlicensed persons, for which the Commission may discipline a licensee.
